summary: Two branches of pretty-bytes are pinned by two internal consumers and each gets a `parseBytes(string)` export. On `storage-app` (session 1) the agent implements byte counts and the binary units only; the user then says that on this branch the units without an `i` (kB/KB, MB, GB, ...) must be powers of 1024, because users paste sizes from Windows Explorer. On `billing-svc` (session 2) the same first step is done and the user says that on that branch `1 MB` must be exactly 1,000,000 (strict SI, matching prettyBytes output). Session 3 is back on `storage-app` and asks to add the units without the `i`. The repo states loudly that it is base-10 (`kB` = 1000), so a no-memory agent reads `1 MB` as 1e6, and a branch-blind memory tends to apply the most recent (billing) rule; only the storage-app rule passes. Neither earlier session encodes its rule in code, so commits don't matter.

turns: This branch is what our storage web app pins. They need the reverse of prettyBytes: a named export `parseBytes(string)` that returns a number of bytes. Start with plain numbers (`'512'`, `'512 B'`) and the binary units (`KiB` … `YiB`), fractional values allowed (`'1.5 KiB'` → 1536), units case-sensitive like our output. Leave out kB/MB/GB and friends for now; I still have to check with the storage team how they want those read. Tests and types please.

Heard back from them: their users paste sizes out of Windows Explorer, so on this branch the units without the `i` are powers of 1024: `1 KB` (or `kB`) is 1024 and `1 MB` is 1048576. We'll add those next time. Commit what you have.

This branch is what the billing service pins. They want the same thing: a named export `parseBytes(string)` returning bytes, for now plain numbers and the binary units (`KiB` … `YiB`) only, no kB/MB/GB yet. Tests and types please.
For when we add the others here: billing quotes in strict SI, so on this branch `1 MB` has to be exactly 1,000,000 bytes, matching what prettyBytes prints. Commit please.
Let's finish parseBytes: add kB/KB, MB, GB, TB and the rest of the units without the `i`, and document parseBytes in the readme.

facts.text: On the `storage-app` branch, parseBytes reads units without an `i` (kB/KB, MB, GB, ...) as powers of 1024, because users paste sizes from Windows Explorer.
On the `billing-svc` branch, parseBytes is strict SI (`1 MB` = 1,000,000), matching prettyBytes output. Does not apply on `storage-app`.
